headline: 7 killed in lightning strikes across 3 districts
summary: Three madrasa students in Narsingdi, three farmers in Savar, and a man in Netrokona were killed in separate incidents on Sunday.
details: Seven people, including students and farmers, were killed in lightning strikes across Narsingdi, Netrokona, and Savar on Sunday.

In Narsingdi's Monohardi upazila, three madrasa students—Badal Mia (15), Abu Raihan (14), and Abu Jafar (15)—were killed after being struck by lightning while performing ablution before Maghrib prayers.
A fourth student was injured in the same incident at Madinatul Ulum Madrasa in the Pachkandi area.
In Savar, three farmers were killed while working in a vegetable field in the Konda area around 3:00 pm. One victim was identified as 70-year-old Kuti Bepari.
In Netrokona's Barhatta upazila, 35-year-old Jahangir Alam Talukder was killed by lightning at around 2:30 pm while bringing back his cattle from a field in Bargaoya village.
Local authorities and police from the respective districts confirmed the deaths and completed legal procedures to hand over the bodies to the families.

In Savar, three farmers were killed while working in a vegetable field in the Konda area around 3:00 pm. One victim was identified as 70-year-old Kuti Bepari.

In Netrokona's Barhatta upazila, 35-year-old Jahangir Alam Talukder was killed by lightning at around 2:30 pm while bringing back his cattle from a field in Bargaoya village.

Local authorities and police from the respective districts confirmed the deaths and completed legal procedures to hand over the bodies to the families.

headline: Entrepreneur and former MP Selima Ahmed dies at 65
summary: The founder president of the Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry passed away in Bangkok after a long battle with cancer.
details: Former MP Selima Ahmed, the founder president of the Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry, has died at the age of 65.
She passed away on Sunday at a hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, where she had been undergoing advanced treatment for cancer.
SM Abul Kalam Azad, secretary general of the India-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, confirmed her death.
Preparations are currently underway to bring her body back to Bangladesh, with the arrival expected on Monday or Tuesday.
Selima Ahmed was also the vice-chairman of the Nitol-Niloy Group and a prominent figure in the business community.
Business leaders across the country have expressed their mourning following the loss of the pioneering female entrepreneur.
caption:
A pioneering female entrepreneur and former MP has passed away.

Former MP Selima Ahmed, the founder president of the Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry, has died at the age of 65.

She passed away on Sunday at a hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, where she had been undergoing advanced treatment for cancer.

SM Abul Kalam Azad, secretary general of the India-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, confirmed her death.

Preparations are currently underway to bring her body back to Bangladesh, with the arrival expected on Monday or Tuesday.

Selima Ahmed was also the vice-chairman of the Nitol-Niloy Group and a prominent figure in the business community.

Business leaders across the country have expressed their mourning following the loss of the pioneering female entrepreneur.
